_comment: Truth table for the stub 'LLM triage service' — keyed by commit hash (the unit of triage). Rationale text simulates what the production LLM (ClaudeTriage) would generate. evt-002's commit is deliberately absent: it is suppressed by the relevance filter and must never reach triage; if it does, the service's failsafe default (needs_human_review) applies.

a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0.vulnerability_class: out-of-bounds read/write in network packet parsing
a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0.reachability_notes: udhcp client parses DHCP responses from the local network segment; runs by default on the GW-7100 WAN interface.
a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0.rationale: [SIMULATED LLM OUTPUT] Two in-scope files changed in this commit, evaluated together: networking/udhcp/dhcpc.c and networking/udhcp/packet.c. The change adds explicit length validation before copying DHCP option payloads and replaces an unchecked offset advance with a bounds-checked iteration. The commit message ('udhcp: tidy option walking') does not mention security, but the diff pattern — new length checks guarding existing copies, no functional change otherwise — is characteristic of a quietly patched parsing vulnerability. Both changed functions handle attacker-supplied packet data.
a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0.recommended_action: Start a candidate rebuild incorporating this commit and schedule regression testing of DHCP client behavior. Treat as pre-disclosure: the fix is public upstream, no advisory exists yet.

9e8d7c6b5a4f3e2d1c0b9a8f7e6d5c4b3a2f1e0d.reachability_notes: net/core/skbuff.c is compiled into the GW-7100 kernel and on the path of all network traffic.
9e8d7c6b5a4f3e2d1c0b9a8f7e6d5c4b3a2f1e0d.rationale: [SIMULATED LLM OUTPUT] One in-scope file changed: net/core/skbuff.c. The commit reorders a pointer assignment relative to a free-and-realloc sequence. This could be a use-after-free fix, or merely a cosmetic reordering with no semantic effect — the surrounding locking makes the race window unclear from the diff alone, and the commit message ('skbuff: simplify clone path') is uninformative. Confidence is insufficient for an automatic verdict in either direction.
9e8d7c6b5a4f3e2d1c0b9a8f7e6d5c4b3a2f1e0d.recommended_action: Route to human review queue. A kernel networking engineer should determine whether the pre-change ordering was exploitable under concurrent clone/free.

2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d.reachability_notes: zutil.c is compiled into the GW-7100 image (zlib 1.3.1).
2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d.rationale: [SIMULATED LLM OUTPUT] One in-scope file changed: zutil.c (CMakeLists.txt is build-system only and not in scope). The change renames internal helper functions and converts K&R-style declarations to ANSI prototypes. No control flow, bounds handling, or data validation is modified; the generated code should be identical. No security relevance to this build.
2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d.recommended_action: None. Verdict and rationale logged for audit.

_failsafe_default.rationale: [STUB FAILSAFE] Commit not present in the demo truth table — defaulting to human review. A triage service must fail safe: an unknown commit is routed to a person, never silently dropped.
